The non-negotiables I hope my child learns before they grow up. 🤍

Not how to be the most obedient.
Not how to get perfect grades.
Not how to make everyone happy.

But how to know their boundaries.
How to say no.
How to understand and express their feelings.
How to be kind without losing themselves.
How to treat people with respect.
And most importantly, how to know they can always come home and tell me the truth.

Because one day, we won’t be there to hold their hand through every situation.

I hope we’ve given them enough confidence, empathy and emotional safety to navigate the world on their own. 💙

Picky eating has been a whole journey in our house 😂

My son was such a great eater, so when my daughter started rejecting almost everything, I was honestly so confused. Some days it felt like every meal was a battle.

Over time, I realised there were a few things I was doing with the best intentions that probably weren’t helping  and that picky eating can have so many different reasons behind it.

So I put together this guide with everything I wish I had known earlier  what picky eating can look like, why it happens, what NOT to do, and what has actually helped us.

The biggest thing I’ve learnt? Consistency over perfection.*🤍

Save this for your next mealtime battle, and send it to a mama who needs it!

Because yes… we’re all just trying to get through one meal at a time. 😂

A lot of moms ask me why I started a moms community, so I thought I’d finally share the little story behind it.

When I became a mom, I realised how much I wanted a space where moms could just talk, ask questions without overthinking, share experiences, make friends and have people who actually understood what they were going through.

With my husband being a pilot and his schedule being quite unpredictable, there were many days when I found myself figuring out motherhood on my own.

And I remember thinking, there must be so many other moms feeling the same way.

So I started a small WhatsApp group. No big plan, just a space for moms to connect.

I never imagined that little group would grow into a community of 2,500+ moms across cities. We meet offline, moms have made genuine friendships and It’s honestly crazy to look back and see how far it has come and I think the best part of this whole journey has been seeing moms who joined as strangers slowly become friends, support each other and create their own little circles.

And that’s probably what makes me the happiest, knowing that something I started from a very personal place has found a place in so many other moms’ lives.

Because we were never meant to figure out motherhood alone.

They say it takes a village to raise a child. I think this is ours. 💙
